title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BERNIE'S STEW
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Bernie Sandoval, a hotel housekeeper from Albuquerque, New Mexico.
Every Sunday she makes green chile stew. Her coworkers call it the best in the state.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FLYER
segments.quote: No one knows what he can do until he tries.
segments.author: Publilius Syrus
lines: One morning, her coworker Dolores taped a flyer to the laundry cart. The state fair stew contest.
Bernie laughed. Me? Against real chefs? I fold towels.
Dolores pointed to a line from Publilius Syrus, an old Roman writer:
No one knows what he can do until he tries.
Bernie signed up before she could change her mind.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: GRANDMA'S RECIPE
segments.quote: Tell me what you eat, and I will tell you what you are.
segments.author: Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin
lines: She called her grandma Lupe in Las Cruces for the recipe.
Grandma said, A handful of this, some of that. Cook it till it smells like Sunday.
Bernie wanted measurements. Grandma quoted the French food writer Brillat-Savarin:
Tell me what you eat, and I will tell you what you are.
So Bernie put away the measuring cups and cooked like herself.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TOO FANCY
segments.quote: In character, in manner, in style, in all things, the supreme excellence is simplicity.
segments.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
lines: Then she got nervous and watched cooking shows.
She added truffle oil, a foam, and one tiny leaf. It tasted like a hotel lobby.
Her neighbor, a retired mailman, read her a line from Longfellow:
In character, in manner, in style, in all things, the supreme excellence is simplicity.
Out went the foam. Back came the pork, the potatoes, and Grandma's chile.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BREAK ROOM
segments.quote: Criticism may not be agreeable, but it is necessary. It fulfils the same function as pain in the human body.
segments.author: Winston Churchill
lines: Before the fair, she brought a pot to the hotel break room and asked for the truth.
Too salty, said one. Not hot enough, said Dolores. Bernie went red as a chile.
Her manager shrugged and quoted Winston Churchill:
Criticism may not be agreeable, but it is necessary. It fulfils the same function as pain in the human body.
So Bernie said thank you and cooked six more pots.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE JUDGE
segments.quote: I don't believe in twisting yourself into knots of excuses and explanations over the food you make.
segments.author: Julia Child
lines: Fair day. Forty cooks in white chef jackets. Bernie wore her hotel polo.
The judge took a bite, and Bernie started apologizing. My stove is small...
Then she remembered Julia Child, her grandma's favorite TV chef:
I don't believe in twisting yourself into knots of excuses and explanations over the food you make.
Bernie closed her mouth, smiled, and let the stew talk.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: SECOND HELPINGS
segments.quote: There is no love sincerer than the love of food.
segments.author: George Bernard Shaw
lines: She took second place, and a ribbon the size of a dinner plate.
That Sunday, she drove the pot to Grandma. Needs salt, Grandma said. Then she ate two bowls.
Bernie thought of the Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw:
There is no love sincerer than the love of food.
Now she cooks every Sunday for Grandma's whole street.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Try it. Cook like yourself. Keep it simple. Hear the truth. Skip the excuses. Share the pot.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Try it. Cook like yourself. Keep it simple. Hear the truth. Skip the excuses. Share the pot.
Me? I made chili once. The fire department gave me a ribbon too.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
